[attribute-std-id]
=== `@std-id` ISO-specific Standard Identifier (for a citation)

In ISO STS, this attribute named the designator for the standard being cited (in the element <<element-std,`<std>`>>). Current NISO STS Best Practice does not use this attribute; rather the identifier for a standard being cited should be tagged either in a <<element-std-id,`<std-id>`>> element (for a single identifier, equivalent to this attribute) or, more typically, using the element <<element-std-id-group,`<std-id-group>`>> which holds several standard identifiers (<<element-std-id,`<std-id>`>>), for example, both a dated and an undated designator.

#### Usage/Remarks
##### NISO STS Best Practice

The information that this <<attribute-std-id,`@std-id`>> attribute conveyed in ISO STS should instead be tagged as element content inside the element <<element-std,`<std>`>>, using either a <<element-std-id,`<std-id>`>> element for one designator or a <<element-std-id-group,`<std-id-group>`>> to record more than one designator. Using an element to hold this designator is preferable because it is frequently necessary to list more than one standard identifier, and an attribute can hold only one. The <<attribute-std-id,`@std-id`>> attribute has been retained for backwards compatibility.

#### OPTIONAL on element:  <<element-std,`<std>`>>

|===
| Value| Meaning

| Text, numbers, or special characters| Provides the designator for the standard being cited (in element <<element-std,`<std>`>>), but Best Practice is not to use this attribute. (See Best Practice above.)
| Restriction| This attribute is optional; there is no default.
|===
